title: Iridium Systems - POC scoping (latency SLOs & benchmarks)
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark harness + workload spec
Customer to provide sample prompts and traffic profile by 2027-07-02
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run (shared infra) week of 2027-07-05
Redwood to send pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot
Security to review SOC2/ISO attachments and confirm KMS requirements
action_items: Alex Kim: Share load generator (k6 scripts) + benchmark plan (due 2027-07-01)
Priya Nair: Prepare initial config for int8/FP16 variants and caching toggles (due 2027-07-03)
Marco Diaz: Provide sample prompt set (100 prompts) and seq length distribution (due 2027-07-02)
Ben Carter: List encryption/KMS and VPC requirements and any audit window needs (due 2027-07-04)
summary: POC scoping focused on latency & throughput SLOs. Customer cares most about TTFT p95 and TPOT p95 targets for chat assistant at expected peak traffic. Agreed measurement plan: 30-min sustained runs + spike/scaling tests on hosted and Dedicated variants, measure p95/p99 for TTFT and per-token latency, and throughput (tokens/sec and concurrent QPS). Next steps: share harness, collect prompts, schedule benchmark run.
topics: Success criteria: TTFT vs TPOT targets
Workload sizing: QPS, concurrency, sequence lengths
Benchmarks: sustained load, spike tests, model variants
Measurement plan: p95/p99, error rates, caching impact
Timeline: 2-week POC schedule and pilot decision criteria
Security and deployment mode: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone good afternoon thanks for joining, we've got about 55 minutes on the agenda to scope the POC for latency SLOs and benchmarks. uh Priya and I will run through measurement plan and then dig into your workload.
00:14 Marco Diaz: Yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. Quick intro - I'm Marco, lead for ML infra at Iridium, Tanya is platform, Ben is security, Lina PM. We want to validate that the assistant can hit production SLAs before committing to Dedicated.
00:30 Alex Kim: Great, can you give us expected traffic and what "hit SLA" looks like for you? TTFT vs TPOT?
00:38 Marco Diaz: Sure. Primary use case is customer support chat. Average prompt ~40 tokens, average response ~120 tokens. Baseline traffic today is about 300 requests per minute (5 rps) but peak can get to 750 rpm (~12.5 rps) during spikes. We want TTFT p95 under 400ms ideally and p99 under 800ms. For per-token (TPOT) we want p95 under 30-40ms/token - basically so chat feels snappy.
01:04 Priya Nair: Good detail - just to clarify TTFT is Time To First Token, TPOT is time per output token, right? We'll measure both. For TPOT we usually report ms/token and also tokens/sec throughput under sustained loads.
01:18 Tanya Li: Also important - we have prefix caching for repeated customer prompts and we use a KV cache in prod. We'd like to see both cold/no-cache and warm/cache results.
01:27 Alex Kim: Makes sense. Our POC typically runs three experiments: 1) functional correctness and cold TTFT baseline, 2) sustained load for 30 minutes to measure p95/p99 and throughput, 3) spike/failure test to validate fallbacks and autoscaling. We'll run each on hosted and Dedicated config and with model quantization variants (FP16 vs int8).
01:47 Marco Diaz: What's realistic on Dedicated latency? People talk about cheaper but slower quantized variants sometimes.
01:50 Priya Nair: Good question. For a 7B-ish model on modern GPUs: FP16 TTFT p95 might be ~250-350ms with good caching and batching; int8 can add small overhead at TTFT sometimes but improve TPOT on longer outputs. We'll quantify. For p99 we're often seeing 2x p95 depending on tail due to autoscaling and cold starts.
02:12 Ben Carter: On security - we need to confirm KMS integration, tenant isolation, audit logs, and data retention. also if we use Dedicated we want to know where logs live.
02:22 Alex Kim: We'll send our security pack. For Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and can push audit logs to your SIEM. We'll include SOC2/ISO docs.
02:29 Marco Diaz: Cool. Back to SLOs - can we make them more concrete? For POC we'll accept: TTFT p95 <= 400ms, TTFT p99 <= 900ms, TPOT p95 <= 40ms/token, and overall error rate <1% under sustained load. If metrics are within 10% of targets we consider it acceptable to proceed to a pilot.
02:51 Alex Kim: That sounds like a reasonable POC success criteria. We'll also provide guidance on how batching impacts these numbers - more batching improves GPU utilization (tokens/second) but can increase TTFT slightly if you wait to form batches.
03:07 Priya Nair: For measurement plan: We'll ask you to provide a representative prompt set (100 prompts) and two traffic profiles: normal and peak. We'll run: warm cache run (with KV/prefix enabled), cold run (no cache), sustained 30-min run at peak QPS, and spike tests (2x peak for 2 minutes). We'll capture TTFT and TPOT histograms and compute p50/p95/p99, plus CPU/GPU utilization and queue times.
03:34 Marco Diaz: How do you simulate multi-tenant noise? Our infra is noisy; we want to know how Redwood's routing/pools perform.
03:40 Priya Nair: We can run a noisy neighbor scenario by adding background synthetic traffic or deploying on shared pool. For Dedicated we can reserve capacity to remove noisy effects. We should test both to show delta.
03:50 Tanya Li: What about sequence lengths? Some prompts go long - up to 400 tokens. That will change TPOT and maybe TTFT for long responses.
03:58 Alex Kim: We'll profile across sequence buckets: short (<64), medium (64-256), long (256-512). We'll report per-bucket p95/p99.
04:07 Marco Diaz: Timeline wise - we want results in two weeks. Is that doable?
04:11 Alex Kim: Yes. Proposed timeline: Day 0 kickoff and collect prompts/traffic (this week), Day 3 Redwood shares harness and config, Day 5 run initial cold/warm tests, Day 8 run sustained + spike tests, Day 10 analyze and share results, Day 14 decision meeting.
04:26 Lina Park: If results fail, is there an option to tune quantization or pick different model sizes?
04:31 Priya Nair: Absolutely - part of the POC is model/quantization sweep. We'll try a smaller faster model and a larger higher-quality one, and test int8 vs FP16. We'll also test prefix caching and batching parameters.
04:45 Ben Carter: On measurement telemetry - will you provide raw histograms? We need them for our SRE team to ingest.
04:50 Alex Kim: Yes, we can export Prometheus-compatible metrics and raw traces. We'll attach the benchmark logs and a CSV/JSON summary.
04:57 Marco Diaz: Anything about function calling or streaming that affects TTFT? We sometimes push structured outputs so streaming first-token is important.
05:04 Priya Nair: Streaming improves perceived latency; TTFT is when first token hits client. For function/tool calls we measure TTFT to first bytes and also end-to-end completion. We'll include both.
05:14 Alex Kim: Ok let's align on concrete numbers in the POC doc: TTFT p95 target 400ms, TTFT p99 900ms, TPOT p95 40ms/token, sustained throughput target to support 750 rpm with <1% errors, and headroom to burst to 2x for 2 minutes. We'll list these as the success criteria.
05:33 Marco Diaz: Sounds good. Any objections about storage of prompts during testing? we prefer not to persist customer data on Redwood side.
05:40 Alex Kim: For POC we can run ephemeral data, or run benchmarks on your VPC/Dedicated environment so no customer data leaves your network. We'll note that in security doc.
05:50 Priya Nair: One more technical: measuring TPOT accurately requires synchronized token timestamps. Our harness records server-side token emission times; client-side network jitter can be filtered out. We'll share the harness instrumentation details.
06:04 Marco Diaz: Good. For success criteria review: if we pass within 10% on TTFT/TPOT and error rates <1% we'll greenlight pilot. If not, we iterate tuning or evaluate Dedicated commit.
06:18 Alex Kim: Great. To recap next steps: Alex shares harness and benchmark plan, Marco shares prompts & traffic profile, Ben confirms security requirements, Priya will prepare model/quantization configs. We'll schedule the benchmark week of July 5th.
06:33 Marco Diaz: Thanks all. Anything else?
06:36 Ben Carter: please include SOC2 attachments and KMS integration doc.
06:39 Alex Kim: Will do. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via calendar invite and attach artifacts.
06:45 (call ends)
